tests: doctor promotes a not-applicable retention to FAIL under --for full and leaves it a WARN under every profile below, in a fleet that tiphys init just created

dangerousStates.find:
status: "WARN",
        detail: `no charter document in ${charterDir}, so no project is realized here yet and retention is not applicable`,
dangerousStates.replace:
status: "PASS",
        detail: `no charter document in ${charterDir}, so no project is realized here yet and retention is not applicable`,

consumesExternalOutput.provenance: Rule (f) is derived per FILE: every member below mutates src/commands/doctor.ts, which spawns `git check-ignore -q` to reach its other retention verdicts, so the capture obligation binds even though the arms these tests guard return BEFORE that spawn. The citation is load-bearing rather than ceremonial: the tests assert that none of the three verdicts downstream of the git-consulting loop (git-ignored, does not exist, present and tracked) appears in the not-applicable line, and the capture is where those verdicts' external contract is recorded (ignored 0, unignored 1, outside a repository 128, git 2.43.0, 2026-08-13). THREE STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT MEMBERS, one per way the promotion can be undone: the condition removed from the `full` list (the state M4-P30 reversed, and the guard that cannot go red), the condition still in the table but attached to a profile below `full` (the promotion inverted rather than deleted, which reddens the arm that says a fresh fleet stays usable below full), and the not-applicable verdict turned into a silent PASS, which defeats the promotion without touching the table at all because only a WARN is ever promoted.
